scope: Characterize the party/group opcode cluster for FFXIV 1.23b. Catalog every dispatcher case body in FUN_004DC690 and FUN_004D8860 that touches Party, Group, or Linkshell wire opcodes; map each opcode to its compact dispatcher-side handler and to the underlying Group::PacketProcessor / SharedWork callee; cross-reference existing BCS-Y entries / receiver_opcode_map_inbound.json / unmapped_payload_decoding.json payload schemas / Group system decomp.

architecture_summary.dual_path_model: FFXIV 1.x routes 'party/group' state-change packets through two dispatchers and three layers. (1) Dispatcher layer: FUN_004DC690 mid-table covers opcodes 0x17A and 0x17C..0x18D; FUN_004D8860 covers 0x0133 GenericData (s2c LuaParam variadic). (2) Compact handler layer (this manifest's primary catalog): each FUN_004DC690 case body is an 8- to 16-byte trampoline at 0x005762x0..0x005763Ax that tail-calls into the Group system at 0x006Cxxxx, except for the special 0x18D PartyMapMarker case which is inlined and the 0x17C GroupHeader case which adds an SEH-protected wrapper around FUN_006CC620. (3) Group system layer: 0x006Cxxxx callees populate the Group::PacketProcessor / SharedWork pipelines documented in docs/group_system_decomp.md. The PacketProcessor uses two parallel subdecoders (sub1 at +0x40, sub2 at +0x94) and fires a combined callback when both complete; SharedWork has 3 parallel 16-byte-stride member arrays (MemberInfo, Property, WorkSync) read via slots 19/20/21 and written via slots 16/17/18.
architecture_summary.wire_runtime_stride_note: Wire format uses 0x30-byte (48) per-member slots that include 32-byte ASCII name + flags + ids; engine post-parse runtime storage uses 16-byte stride. These are intentional - the wire carries human-readable names for the UI; the runtime keeps id-keyed lookup tables. Group decomp confirms no conflict between the two strides.
architecture_summary.chat_path: The party/linkshell chat opcode 0x00C9 (PartyChat - c2s WorldServerbound; s2c WorldClientbound) is structurally separate from the Group::PacketProcessor pipeline. C2s emission is cataloged as BCS-Y-0309 (ChatOutbound_PartyChat_emitter_FUN_004DF6D0 - 536-byte body via Chat generic forwarder BCS-Y-0306). S2c receive lives in the Chat channel callback, not in the Zone dispatcher.
architecture_summary.c2s_party_command_path: The actor-facing party commands (PartyInvite, PartyLeave, PartyModify/Kick/ChangeLeader, PartyResign, PartyBreakup) are not direct client-side opcode emitters. They are issued as Lua console commands (Data/scripts/commands/Party*Command.lua) that go through the GenericDataPacket opcode 0x0133 LuaParam pipeline server-side, then mapped on the map server to internal 0x10XX Map<->World bus opcodes. These are NOT actual ZoneProtoChannel wire opcodes; the 1.23b client never sends or receives them directly. Confirmed by xivl-opcodes:data/bahamut_gaps.json.
architecture_summary.0x0133_directionality: 0x0133 carries TWO distinct semantics by direction. C2s (MapServerbound, named GroupCreated, BCS-Y-bound to OP_RX_GROUP_CREATED) - client tells server 'I created group X via /_init'. S2c (UserData via FUN_004D8860 case 0x133) - server pushes a LuaParam-encoded variadic RPC to a Lua handler keyed by class-name (e.g. 'attention' -> attentionMessage Lua callback). The s2c 0x0133 is fundamentally different from the s2c 0x017A SynchGroupWorkValues path despite both touching 'group' state.

key_findings: All 11 s2c Group/Content member opcodes (0x17C-0x186) plus 0x17A SynchGroupWorkValues, 0x187 SetOccupancyGroup, 0x188-0x189 CreateNamedGroup, 0x18A SetActiveLinkshell, and 0x18B SetGroupLayoutId share the SAME dispatcher case-body shape in FUN_004DC690 mid-table (0x13D < uVar2 branch). 16 of them are 8-byte trampolines into the Group::PacketProcessor / SharedWork helpers at 0x006C2Fxx-0x006CDxxx. Only 0x17C (109-byte SEH wrapper) and 0x18D (232-byte inline handler with a nonzero +0x4d8 gate) break the trampoline pattern.

0x18D PartyMapMarkerUpdate is the ARCHITECTURAL ODD ONE OUT in this cluster: it does NOT touch the Group::PacketProcessor / SharedWork pipeline. Its inline handler at FUN_00575550 gates on `*(int*)(zone+0x4d8) != 0` (a nonzero zone-owned gate whose lifecycle and semantic name remain unresolved), reads the marker count from a non-standard offset (packet+0x18 instead of part of the payload header), and forwards through FUN_006C1570 / FUN_00573F10 to a UI/rendering update path. receiver_discovery.json correctly classifies this as direct_non_receiver_handler, distinct from the other group_sharedwork_non_receiver classifications.

0x0133 has DUAL semantics by direction. C2s = GroupCreated (client tells server it acknowledged a group). S2c = GenericDataPacket / UserData (server pushes Lua-VM variadic RPC). The c2s side is the ONLY c2s opcode in this cluster that the client emits (PartyInvite/PartyLeave/PartyModify are Lua-console-driven, going through the GenericData LuaParam path on the c2s side as well). 0x017A SynchGroupWorkValues is the s2c response payload associated with the 0x0133 c2s GroupCreated confirm.

0x00C9 PartyChat goes through the Chat channel, NOT the Zone channel. C2s emitter is BCS-Y-0309 (already cataloged). S2c receive handler is in the Chat channel callback (out of scope for this manifest's FUN_004DC690/FUN_004D8860 focus).

No client-side equivalent of PartyInvite/PartyLeave/PartyModify exists as a direct wire opcode. The Lua commands Data/scripts/commands/Party*Command.lua (PartyInviteCommand, PartyKickCommand, PartyLeaderCommand, PartyResignCommand, PartyDisbandCommand, PartyBreakupCommand, PartyTargetCommand, addtoparty.lua) all go through the Lua-VM bindings (Application::Lua::Script::Client::Control::GroupBase 15 client-side methods) and are relayed by the server. The internal Map<->World bus values are NOT actual ZoneProtoChannel wire opcodes (confirmed by bahamut_gaps.json).
The survey identified 20 function candidates and four Group::* RTTI class candidates. Canonical promotion status and identifiers are determined by symbols.json.

Group::PacketProcessor dual-subdecoder architecture (finding) explains why GroupHeader (0x17C) + GroupMembersBegin (0x17D) + GroupMembersX08-X64 (0x17F-0x182) + GroupMembersEnd (0x17E) are emitted as a TRIO/QUARTET in a single sequenceId burst. The PacketProcessor's sub*_complete flags + +0xEA both_callback_pending guards mean the combined callback only fires when BOTH subdecoders complete.

group_system_decomp.md 'open question' about runtime registration of ZoneProtoDownCallbackInterface is RESOLVED in network_dispatch_dual_paths.md: there IS no runtime registration. The dispatcher uses DummyCallback whose per-opcode slots are 3-byte `ret 0xc` stubs. Group-family opcodes (0x017A / 0x0133 IN / 0x017C-F / 0x0183) are consumed by Group::PacketProcessor's queue-walk + dual subdecoder, NOT by per-opcode vtable callbacks. This is why FUN_004DC690 dispatches them DIRECTLY (bypassing the ZoneProtoChannel dispatch table) - the FUN_005763xx trampolines are the client's actual handlers.
open_questions: 0x0143 DeleteGroup now reaches a confirmed Group::BreakupBuilder command, but the exact Group registry entry and SharedWork state removed by that command remain unresolved.

FUN_006CD790 (0x188 CreateNamedGroup callee) and FUN_006CD7B0 (0x189 CreateNamedGroupMultiple callee) are in a different cluster from the SharedWork append callees (0x006C2Fxx-0x006C31xx). What is the group-registry data structure these write into? Likely the per-zone groups list in zone+0x???? (separate from the per-group SharedWork instances). Needs reverse search of writes to whatever array FUN_006CD790 touches.
0x017A property-stream MurmurHash2 ids - the property path -> id mapping in gam-property-registry.md should be cross-validated against the s2c property writes observed in pcap.

0x18B SetGroupLayoutId - the exact semantics of the fields at offsets +20 and +21 remain unresolved; the current names are layoutKind and unknown2. Resolution needs expanded pcap correlation across more captures.

What is the lifecycle and semantic name of the zone-owned nonzero gate at +0x4d8 used by 0x18D PartyMapMarkerUpdate? Fresh retail evidence found no zone-owned writer or pointer assignment; the field should not be called an active-map-widget pointer without new evidence. Useful for understanding why retail emits 0x18D so heavily (592x across 38 captures).
Is there a c2s opcode that the client sends when it OPENS the party UI / map UI? Searching FUN_004DF6D0's neighbors (Chat outbound emitters) or the Zone outbound Tier-C list may surface it.
